Appeal under
Section 41
of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against order dated 02.05.2023 passed by       District       Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, U.T. Chandigarh in Consumer Complaint No.519/2021.

 

 

 

BEFORE:       MRS. PADMA PANDEY, PRESIDING MEMBER
Mr.PREETINDER SINGH,MEMBER

 

 

 

Argued by:      Sh.Jasbir Singh Tiwana, appellant in person.
Sh.Shashank Shekhar Sharma,  advocate for                                      respondents   No.1 & 2.

 

                         Sh. Ram Pal Kohle, Advocate for respondent No.3

 

 

   PER PADMA PANDEY, PRESIDING MEMBER
This appeal is directed against the order dated 02.05.2023, rendered by the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission-I, U.T. Chandigarh (hereinafter to be referred as "the Ld. Lower Commission"), vide which, it dismissed the complaint, being devoid of any merit.
2.     Before the Ld. Lower Commission, it was case of the complainant/appellant that he being  a senior citizen  and suffering from various diseases, his movements as well as breathing capacity is seriously impaired, thus it was necessary for him to travel  by business class as the herniated discs does not permit him to travel sitting up straight for long period of time. Accordingly the complainant   booked a return ticket via Emirates airlines business class vide booking reference No.CZVDDB and he departed from New Delhi to New Jersey on  10th of January 2020 with scheduled booked returned ticket for  27th may 2020 vide light number EK0210.  Copy of ticket is C-1.  The complainant paid a sum of Rs.2,98,000/- to  OP No.3 for booking of  the ticket. It is alleged that the OPs No.1 & 2 airlines about two months before the scheduled return journey, unilaterally cancelled the flight and intimated the complainant through an email. Subsequently there was no further communication from them  for the next 3-4 months and kept the appellant in dark which left the appellant in complete shock and under grave mental stress being stranded in a foreign country, with depleting medical supplies, and money.   Since no clarification was received from OPs No.1&2 regarding future travel plan, therefore, the complainant under compelling circumstances purchased emergency ticket from United Airlines for returning back India, which cost the complainant to the tune of Rs.2,22,740/- for one way journey The appellant had to spent the said amount inspite of having booked and pre-paid for the return ticket with respondents No.1 & 2 much in advance. On coming back to India, the appellant  asked for refund from Opposite Parties  No.1&2  but they only refunded Rs.67,286/- to the complainant though they themselves unilaterally cancelled the flight.  The complainant also sent legal notice to Opposite Parties  No.1&2 but to no effect. Hence,  alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the part of the Opposite Parties, a consumer complaint was filed before the Ld. Lower Commission.
3.                Pursuant to issuance of notice,  Opposite Parties NO.1&2 appeared and contested the complaint. In their reply, it was admitted that the complainant booked Business Class tickets to travel on Sectors Delhi-Dubai-Newark and return. It was  stated that the return ticket of the complainant was cancelled on account of nationwide COVID 19 lockdown imposed by the Government of India on 25th march 2020 and consequent ban on operation of all domestic and international flights that was imposed by the Director General of Civil Aviation, Government of India vide circular in continuation No.4/1/2020 IR.  It was further stated that not only  the  return ticket  booked by the complainant for travel on 27.5.2020 was cancelled but all bookings scheduled for and after 25.3.2020 had to be cancelled by all airline operators in compliance with the   government notification in force and not for any fault on the part of Opposite Parties No.1&2.  It was further stated that "Transport Bubbles" or "Special Air Travel Arrangements" were made under bilateral agreements between the government of India and USA as such Opposite Parties being neither an Indian Airlines nor a US Airline could provide a ticket to the complainant for travel to India from USA.  Thereafter, refund of Rs.69,713/- was allowed  to the complainant as per applicable law and procedure. It was further stated that price of a return ticket i.e. a ticket for both onward   and   return journey is cheaper than two separate tickets for onward journey and the return journey on the same sectors. Therefore, refund of the unutilized portion of the ticket       ( return journey) is not half the price paid but a lesser amount.  Denying other allegations in the complaint, a prayer was made for dismissal of the complaint.
4.                Opposite Party No.3  also appeared before the Ld. Lower Commission and filed reply. In its reply, OP NO.3  stated that its role is restricted only to the extent of issuance of tickets and in no manner connected with the operation of the flights, as such it cannot be held responsible for the cancellation of the flights. Denying all other allegations made in the complaint, a prayer was made for dismissal of the complaint.  However, subsequently   OP No.3 did not turn up before the Ld. Lower Commission and  vide order dated 17.03.2023 it was proceeded against exparte.
5.                  On appraisal of the complaint, and the evidence adduced on record, Ld. Lower Commission did not find merit in the complaint and dismissed the same.
6.                Aggrieved against the  aforesaid order passed by the Ld. Lower Commission, the instant Appeal  has been filed by the Appellant/Complainant  for setting aside the impugned order by granting relief as claimed in the complaint.
7.                  We have heard  the appellant in person, Counsel for the respondents, and have gone through the evidence and record of the case with utmost care and circumspection.
8.                  In the appeal, the ground taken by the appellant is that the conduct of the airline in cancelling the flight is not to blame, it is only their post cancellation behavior and attitude which was severely deficient.  According to the appellant, there was no one way ticket involved  as it was a single contract and has to be performed in entirety and cannot be broken into segments for convenience. Further the tickets prices shoot up on Christmas eve or new year's even as ticket costs are determined by supply and demand, as such it cannot be said that cost of return ticket is always less.  The appellant vehemently contended that the Ld. Lower Commission while passing the impugned order has not considered the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in
Pravasi Legal Cell & Ors. Vs Union of India & Ors
CWP(C)  No.570 of 2020 etc. wherein it is specifically mentioned that refund should be of the money collected from the passenger without any cuts.
9.                  There is no denying the fact that the appellant travelled on the sectors Delhi-Dubai and Dubai Newark as scheduled but was unable to utilize his return tickets as the filights in May,2020 had to be cancelled on account of COVID 19 pandemic during which all scheduled international flights were globally suspended. It is also an admitted that the appellant has been refunded Rs.67,286/- on 14.9.2020. The appellant has claimed refund of cost of the ticket booked by him to travel back to India. Admittedly the return flights were cancelled on account of government advisories and notifications as a consequence of COVID 19 pandemic and not  on account of any deficiency or negligence on the part of the respondents. The appellant was originally scheduled to travel back to Delhi on the flights of the respondents in May,2020 but he had to  take a  direct flight from New York to Delhi on 16.9.2020 as the flights of the respondents were not operating due to Covid 19.
10.                 The Judgment cited by the appellant in the case titled
Pravasi Legal Cell & Ors. Vs Union of India & Ors
(Supra) was pronounced by the  Hon'ble Supreme Court on 1.10.2020 whereas refund has already been processed by the respondents on 14.09.2020 that is even before
the said judgment
was pronounced mandating refund to the passengers where bookings were made by the passengers and to the travel agents in cases where bookings were made by the travel agents. As per  finding given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court  "if a   passenger has booked a ticket during the  lockdown period( from 25th March,2020 to 24th May,2020) for travel during lockdown period and the airline has received payment for booking of air ticket for travel during the same period for both domestic and international air travel and the refund is sought by the passenger against that booking being cancelled, the airline shall refund the full amount collected without any cancellation charges. The refund shall be made within a period of three weeks from the date of cancellation." However, in the instant case the appellant travelled from New Delhi to New Jersey on 10.1.2020. Thus, he booked the ticket before the lockdown period. Further, as per the aforesaid judgment, "passengers who booked tickets at any period of time but for travel after 24th May- refund of fares to the passengers covered under this category shall be governed by the provisions of Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR)". Return journey of the appellant was scheduled for 27.5.2020 i.e. after 24th May,2020, as such refund was applicable as per provisions of Civil Aviation requirement.  As stated by the respondents, no cancellation fee was charged  and the refund was made as per provisions of CAR.
11.             As regards the quantum of refund, the Ld. Lower Commission rightly observed that the ticket issued to  a passenger by an airline comprises of  two components, the fare and the taxes. The taxes are payable to the government of the country of origin and the country of destination and most taxes become payable as soon as the ticket is utilized for travel on the first sector itself. Therefore, upon cancellation after partial utilization, the refund in respect of the taxes is never 50%. Moreover, the cost of a one-way ticket is always more than the cost of a return ticket and the fare component for the onward travel is also never the same as the fare component for the return travel. Therefore, the refund of the fare component after partial utilization is also not 50% in case the ticket is utilized for onward travel but not for return travel. The Ld. Lower Commission further observed from   comparison  of prices of one-way and return tickets as  given in Exhibit R-1/4 that the price of a one-way trip from Delhi to New York as on 30.09.2020 was about INR 1,62,640 whereas the cost of a return ticket from Delhi to New York and back on 30.09.2020 was INR 2,44,846. Thus, one can see that the cost of one-way travel is much more than half of the cost of the return travel for the same sectors.
12.             We find that the order passed by the Ld. District Commission is based on correct appreciation of   evidence and law on the point and does not suffer from illegality and perversity warranting any interference of this Commission.
13.                   For the reasons recorded above, the appeal, being devoid of merit, must fail, and the same is dismissed,   with no order as to costs. The order of the Ld. Lower Commission is upheld.
14.       Certified copies of this order be sent to the parties free of charge.
15.                     The file be consigned to Record Room, after completion.
